title: Primary floor head rollers do not power on. Small canister, top heavy
text:
Primary floor head rollers do not power on. Small canister, top heavy. I'm a vacuum expert at this point. We've never had fewer than four house dogs at once in the past twenty years. That means I vacuum daily and mop floors & dust every other day so we don't live in a hair ridden, dog smelling hovel. There's no excuse for a home to smell like dogs or for dog hair to cling to people's clothing. A really good vacuum or two is a necessity in this house.

I typically burn out a vacuum cleaner every year. The only ones that haven't succumbed to the daily dog hair and regular dirt are the shop vac, the big Dyson and the Dyson cordless. I actually prefer the cordless flexibility of the two year old Dyson and hoped this Hoover Fusion would work as well. Not even a little bit.

The direct comparison is like having a toy next to the Dyson. First thing is that the Hoover is top heavy and not well balanced. No way do I want to hold this thing upright and try to clean the ceiling fans or upper corners. The second problem is that I have to remove the battery to charge it up - my Dyson cordless plugs in directly in the hanging cradle with one step. Third issue is the small canister - it's suitable for random, light dirt quick pick up only.

My main problem though is the non-operational rollers. They will not turn on and the digital status light on the handle shows a constant yellow warning or is blank. The machine powers on and can be used with the small attachments like the crevice tool etc. But the primary floor head does not work on mine.
